summary.short: Executive Order of October 30, 2023 directs federal agencies on safe, secure and trustworthy AI development and use. It requires developers of potential dual-use foundation models and owners of large computing clusters to report specified information to the Commerce Secretary, and sets compute thresholds for that reporting. It also directs guidance, standards, studies, and rules on federal AI use, privacy, workers, civil rights and sectors.
summary.long: Executive Order of October 30, 2023 directs executive departments and agencies to govern AI development and use under eight stated principles. Section 4 requires the Commerce Secretary to require companies developing potential dual-use foundation models, and entities possessing large-scale computing clusters, to report specified information, using compute thresholds above 10^26 integer or floating-point operations (and 10^23 for primarily biological sequence data). It also directs proposed rules requiring US infrastructure-as-a-service providers to report foreign training runs and to verify foreign resellers' customers. NIST is to develop AI safety guidance, including red-teaming, and Section 4.4 directs biosecurity measures for synthetic nucleic acids. Section 4.5 addresses labeling and provenance of synthetic content. Other sections cover innovation and talent (5), workers (6), equity and civil rights, including criminal justice and benefits (7), sector guidance for health, transportation, education and communications (8), privacy (9), and federal government AI use through OMB guidance, Chief AI Officers, minimum risk-management practices and procurement (10). Most deadlines run from 30 to 540 days after the order's date. Section 13 states that the order creates no enforceable rights and is subject to applicable law and appropriations.
